_comment: Programme detail researched from official awarding-body sources and applied by the programme_details stage. Only empty record fields are filled; a value already present is never overwritten here.
_rules: Every record must carry verification.source_citations, or the stage skips it entirely. An amount with nothing to check it against is worse than no amount, because it looks researched.
fully_funded is applied only when tuition_coverage is true, so a stipend can never be recorded as though it were a tuition waiver.
Official facts live in official_details; guidance derived from them lives in applicant_utility. They are stored apart and must never be merged.
A field the awarding body does not publish stays null. Absence of evidence is an answer, not a gap to be filled by inference.
deadline_central is the programme's own closing date. deadline_institutional is any earlier university date, stored separately.

official.description: The France Excellence Eiffel scholarship is a French Ministry of Foreign Affairs programme managed by Campus France that funds tuition fees plus a monthly allowance for students from non-European Economic Area countries studying in France at under 25 (master's) or under 30 (doctoral). Candidates are selected and nominated by French institutions, which build a master list of excellence of up to three candidates per scheme and discipline. Campus France makes the payments, and the scheme does not cover housing, health insurance or transport.
official.program_type: Government scholarship
official.coverage: Covers tuition fees and a monthly allowance of EUR 1,181 (master's) or EUR 1,426 (doctoral), but not housing, health insurance or transport.

official.application_cycle: Annual, coordinated with the applicant university (typically applications open in the spring/summer preceding the study year)
official.deadline_central_display: No central date. The Deutschlandstipendium is coordinated by the applicant university, and each university sets its own application period, which it publishes on its own website.
official.deadline_note: The official site is explicit: 'You will find the current application period on the website of the university where you want to apply.' There is no central closing date; admission office deadlines differ by university and are published locally.

official.funding_duration: 12 months, up to 24 months for master's courses
official.tuition_coverage_note: The Deutschlandstipendium is a monthly stipend only. The official FAQ addresses this directly: it is a scholarship for excellent students and does not include tuition fees or a travel allowance. The FAQ recommends checking the financing options of the chosen university and other bodies for help with study and travel costs.
official.funding_label: Deutschlandstipendium - EUR 300 per month for 12 months (up to 24 for master's)

12 months normally, extendable to 24 months for master's courses

official.international_eligibility: Explicitly for international students: applicants must be able to migrate to Germany to study, and the scheme is funded by the German Foreign Office together with partner institutions and private donors.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Coordinated by the applicant university, which also defines subject priorities; the German Foreign Office provides the funding.
official.application_method: Apply through the university. Two variants are described: the university selects the scholarship holders (Auswahlverfahren der Hochschule), or the university forwards suitable students and the DAI decides (Dai procedure). The application forms are not issued by the Deutschlandstipendium website; the university publishes them.

official.description: The Deutschlandstipendium is funded by the German Foreign Office with around 900 scholarships for excellent international students each year. It pays EUR 300 per month for 12 months, extendable to 24 months for master's students, plus insurance contributions. Applications are made directly to the university, which publishes its own application period, forms and subject-specific criteria, and either selects the scholars itself or forwards candidates for the DAI to decide. Eligibility requires being admitted to a German university and migrating to Germany to study.
official.program_type: Government scholarship
official.coverage: A EUR 300 monthly stipend for 12 months (up to 24 for master's) plus insurance contributions; it does not cover tuition fees or travel.

official.description: The Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students is a JASSO programme for international students already enrolled in Japan at undergraduate schools, graduate schools, junior colleges, colleges of technology, specialized training colleges, university preparatory courses or Japanese language institutes who have excellent academic and character records and face financial difficulties. It pays JPY 48,000 per month at graduate and undergraduate level, or JPY 30,000 at Japanese language institutes, for 12 months or 6 months. Applications are made through the enrolled educational institution, which nominates candidates to JASSO.
official.program_type: Government-funded scholarship for privately-financed international students already studying in Japan, distributed through educational institutions
official.coverage: Provides a monthly stipend of JPY 48,000 (graduate and undergraduate level) or JPY 30,000 (Japanese language institutes) for 12 months or 6 months. Tuition fees, enrolment fees, travel and housing are not addressed on the page and are not covered by the published stipend.

official.application_cycle: Annual cycle keyed to Korean graduate school admission: graduate school admission around November, recommendation submitted by the graduate school around December, Foundation interview around January, final selection announcement around February, certificate award ceremony in March
official.deadline_institutional: Admission to a Master's or Doctoral programme at a Korean graduate school, on that university's own timetable, with the graduate school submitting the recommendation to the Foundation in December.
official.deadline_note: There is no applicant-facing application deadline, because applicants do not apply to the Foundation. The published selection procedure is a monthly institutional cycle: graduate school admission (~Nov), recommendation submission by the graduate school (~Dec), Foundation interview (~Jan), final selection announcement (~Feb) and certificate award ceremony (Mar). The binding dates are therefore the Korean university's admission deadline and its internal recommendation submission to the Foundation in December.
official.status_note: Read on 1 October 2026. The selection procedure places the cycle in its early stages, with graduate school admission and recommendation submission expected in November and December 2026 and the final announcement around February 2027. The Foundation publishes no application window of its own.

official.description: The DAAD Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS) programme funds foreign graduates from development and newly industrialised countries who have at least two years' professional experience to take a postgraduate or Master's degree, and in exceptional cases a doctoral degree, at a state or state-recognised German university. Scholarships are awarded individually for courses on the DAAD's published list of postgraduate courses, last between 12 and 42 months depending on the programme, and applications are made directly to the chosen course rather than to the DAAD.
official.program_type: Government/DAAD development scholarship for postgraduate study and, exceptionally, doctorates
official.coverage: Covers a monthly payment of EUR 992 (graduates) or EUR 1,300, rising to EUR 1,400 from February 2026 (doctoral candidates), insurance cover and a travel allowance; rent subsidies and family allowances may be added under certain circumstances. No tuition waiver is stated.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country appears on the published DAC list of eligible countries
Confirm your degree is no more than six years old and you have at least two years of post-Bachelor professional experience
Confirm you have not resided in Germany for more than 15 months at the application deadline
Pick up to three EPOS-listed courses and rank them in the application form
Prepare ONE uniform motivation letter covering all three courses and the ranking
Get your employer's recommendation letter on official letterhead, signed, stamped and dated
Get your employment certificate covering at least two years after the Bachelor's degree
Book IELTS or TOEFL early; the institutional TOEFL is not accepted
If you studied in the People's Republic of China, arrange the APS certificate
Apply directly to each course by that course's own deadline, not to the DAAD
common_rejection_risks: Sending the application to the DAAD instead of the course, which will not be forwarded
Submitting different motivation letters per course, which breaches the uniform-letter rule
Failing to prioritise the three courses consistently between form and letter
Having resided in Germany for more than 15 months at the deadline
Degrees older than six years without a strong justification
Missing the DSH 2 or TestDaF 4 requirement for a German-taught course
Submitting an incomplete application, which cannot be considered
Submitting in a language other than English or German
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees, if the chosen course is not fee-free
Living costs above the monthly payment, including any shortfall not covered by a rent subsidy
Travel not covered by the travel allowance or by the home country
Visa and immigration costs
Family costs beyond the conditional accompanying-family allowance
document_audit: Check the EPOS checklist is completed and signed
Check the CV uses the europass template and has no unexplained gaps
Check the employment certificate covers at least two years after the Bachelor's degree and is current
Check degree certificates have certified translations where not in German or English
Check the transcript includes an explanation of the grading system

alerts.message: Changing the priority order in the application form after submission is not permitted; the DAAD warns this can lead to withdrawal of an awarded scholarship.
You cannot pass DSH or TestDaF without prior German at least at B1, so the six-month preparatory course does not exempt you from that baseline.
There is no DAAD-wide deadline; use the DAAD PDF of course deadlines for 2027/2028 and each course's website.

submission_workflow: Check eligibility against the DAC country list and the six-year degree rule
Choose up to three EPOS-listed postgraduate courses and rank them
Download and complete the signed checklist and the EPOS application form
Write one uniform motivation letter covering course choice and prioritisation
Request the employer recommendation letter and employment certificate
Obtain language certificates and certified translations
Submit directly to each chosen course by that course's deadline
If proposed by the course's selection committee, upload the full application to the DAAD Portal

official.application_cycle: Three calls per year; 2026 calls opened 15 March, 15 July and 15 November 2026
official.deadline_central_display: Calls open on 15 March, 15 July and 15 November; once a call has reached the maximum number of currently 800 applications, the application round will be closed.
official.deadline_note: There is no fixed closing date. Since 2026 the Foundation runs three calls annually, each opening approximately eight months before its selection meeting, and 'Once a call has reached the maximum number of currently 800 applications, the application round will be closed'. As at 1 October 2026 the current call has already reached its maximum, so no new applications can be created; the next call opens 15 November 2026.
official.status_note: The page states: 'We have received the maximum number of applications for the current call. Therefore, unfortunately, no new applications can be created at present. The next call will open on November 15, 2026.'
official.funding_duration: Postdocs: 6 to 24 months, divided into up to three stays within three years. Experienced researchers: 6 to 18 months, divided into up to three stays within three years.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Not addressed. The fellowship is a research sponsorship for a research stay, not enrolment funding, and no tuition statement is published.
official.funding_label: Monthly fellowship: EUR 3,000 for postdocs, EUR 3,600 for experienced researchers
benefits: Monthly fellowship amount of EUR 3,000 for postdocs plus additional benefits
Monthly fellowship amount of EUR 3,600 for experienced researchers plus additional benefits
A two- to four-month intensive German language course immediately prior to the research fellowship
Family benefits for children and partners
Subsidies for private full health insurance
Allowances for travel expenses: 'If the fellow's own institution does not cover travel expenses, the Humboldt Foundation will pay a single lump sum for return travel'
Personal support throughout the sponsorship
Flexible determination of the fellowship start date
Research costs subsidy to the host institution: EUR 800 per month for natural sciences and engineering, EUR 500 per month for humanities or social sciences
Alumni programmes after the research stay, including return fellowships
eligibility: Postdocs: completed the doctorate or equivalent academic qualification during the last four years, or will complete it before the envisaged selection meeting and can provide a written summary of findings
Postdocs: published in academic journals and by publishing houses reviewed according to international standards
Experienced researchers: completed the doctorate during the last twelve years

Experienced researchers: academic profile substantiated by an extensive list of publications including important papers in which you acted as thematic lead, and hold a leadership role commensurate with your career level (for example assistant professor, lecturer, head of an independent research group or higher)
If a doctorate in the field or country of origin is not possible or uncommon, applicants can apply up to 16 years after a master's or other postgraduate degree with a commensurate publication record

Nationality: 'You are not a German national.' German nationals, or those who obtained their university entrance qualification and degree, or degree and doctorate, in Germany, may apply only if they have lived and worked abroad for more than ten years and intend to continue doing so long-term, or for more than five years with a strong connection to their current country of residence
Stay: must not have lived in Germany for longer than a total of 90 days within the 18-month period prior to submitting the application
Must have a mentoring agreement and written confirmation of research facilities from a host at a German academic institution, plus a detailed host review
Must be able to provide two expert reviews
Must not have already received sponsorship directly from the Humboldt Foundation (research fellowship or award)
Hosts may not be in a close personal (marriage or civil partnership) or familial (parents, siblings, children) relationship with the applicant
official.citizenship_residency: 'The Humboldt Research Fellowship for researchers of all nationalities and research areas'. Excludes German nationals and educational residents unless they have lived and worked abroad for more than ten years (or more than five years with a strong connection to their current country of residence).
official.international_eligibility: Explicit: all nationalities and research areas, with a mobility (residence) rule rather than a citizenship restriction.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All fields and research areas are eligible. Language requirements differ by discipline: natural sciences and engineering need good German or English; humanities, social sciences and medicine need good German if necessary for the research, otherwise good English. Physicians whose research involves patients must have a good knowledge of German.
official.application_method: Submit the necessary documents to the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation online only. The application is automatically forwarded to the host, who uploads their documents; the application is only forwarded to the Foundation once the host has submitted all necessary documents. Applications cannot be submitted before the expert reviewers have uploaded their reviews, and only while the portal is open.
requirements: Meet the career-stage condition: postdoc within four years of the doctorate, experienced researcher within twelve years (with the 16-year rule where no doctorate is customary)
Not be a German national or educational resident, unless the long-term foreign residence conditions are met
Not have lived in Germany for more than a total of 90 days in the 18 months before submitting
Secure a host at a German university or research institution who provides a mentoring agreement, written confirmation of research facilities and a detailed review

Provide two expert reviews uploaded by the reviewers themselves in a protected area (postdocs: doctoral supervisor and one other researcher outside your institute where possible; experienced researchers: collaborative partners and/or researchers, preferably outside your country of origin)
Upload a CV of two pages maximum and a research outline of five pages maximum
Upload the complete list of publications and a list of selected key publications using the provided samples
Upload a doctoral certificate or proof of completed doctorate, or confirmation that the doctorate will be completed before the selection meeting
Upload a German language certificate if required
Apply within an open call window and before the 800-application cap closes the round
documents: Curriculum vitae (two pages max)
Research outline (five pages max)
Complete list of your publications
List of selected key publications
Key publications
Doctoral certificate or proof of completed doctorate, or confirmation of completion before the selection meeting
German language certificate, if required
If required: publisher's acceptance notifications and/or acknowledgement of receipt, and summaries or translations of key publications not available in German or English
Two expert reviews, uploaded personally by the expert reviewers
A detailed statement of your host in Germany and a confirmation of research facilities
official.english_requirement_note: No English certificate is required: 'I have worked in an English-speaking country for several years. Do I need an English language certificate? No, an English language certificate is not required.' A German language certificate is required only where German is necessary for the research; natural scientists and engineers need good German or English, and no certificate is required if English or German is your native language.
selection_criteria: Academic career and academic record to date (mobility, determination, thematic scope, academic productivity)
Quality of the key publications named in the application (originality, innovativeness, evaluation of your own contributions to publications involving several authors)

Originality and innovative potential of the proposed research (significance for the further development of the subject area, convincing selection of scientific methods, potential for scientific development, clear focus and feasibility within the requested sponsorship period, viability at the host institute)
Future potential (academic potential, personal development, career prospects, e.g. professorial appointment)
Independent research profile (for experienced researchers)
The assessment also considers the individual life journey and educational background, in terms of equal opportunities and accessibility
Approval rate: 'Looking ahead to the upcoming meetings of the selection committee, we expect that 20 - 25% of the applications received will be approved'
official.duration: Postdocs: 6 to 24 months. Experienced researchers: 6 to 18 months. Fellowships can be divided into up to three stays within three years, and a minimum stay of six months must be applied for (which can be divided into two blocks of three months).
award_holder_conditions: Start the fellowship no less than two and no more than twelve months after the selection meeting
Complete any required doctorate before commencing the research fellowship
Comply with the rules of good scientific practice and scientific ethics
Report additional earnings from freelance work, employment or fellowships in the country where a research stay outside Germany takes place; these will usually be deducted from the fellowship amount

Conduct research outside Germany only under stated conditions: the project must be carried out at the German host institute for at least six months and time outside Germany should usually not exceed 25% of the expected total funding period
Research stays outside Germany at the very beginning or end of the funding period are permitted only in exceptional cases
Extra earnings from the host country during a research stay outside Germany must be reported and usually deducted
If appointed at a university abroad, requests for continued use of awarded funds are reviewed case by case under the 'Money follows Researcher' conditions
supplements_or_initiatives: Programme is part of the Global Minds Initiative Germany of the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space
CAPES-Humboldt Research Fellowship for researchers from Brazil
Alexander von Humboldt Professorship
Alumni programmes, including return fellowships and later visits to Germany
Host institute research cost allowance of EUR 800 per month (natural sciences and engineering) or EUR 500 per month (humanities and social sciences)
official.description: The Humboldt Research Fellowship sponsors researchers with above-average qualifications from all countries to conduct a 6 to 24 month research stay in Germany, with EUR 3,000 per month for postdocs and EUR 3,600 for experienced researchers. Applicants need a host at a German institution, two expert reviews, and a career-stage and mobility match, and the fellowship includes an intensive German language course before the stay plus family, health insurance and travel support. Since 2026 the Foundation runs three calls a year, each closing automatically when 800 applications are received.
official.program_type: International research fellowship for postdoctoral and mid-career researchers
official.coverage: Covers a monthly fellowship (EUR 3,000 postdocs / EUR 3,600 experienced researchers), a pre-stay language course, family allowances, private health insurance subsidy and a single lump sum for return travel where the home institution does not cover it. It does not fund tuition, and living costs beyond the fellowship plus listed allowances are not covered.

Confirm your career stage: within four years of the doctorate for postdocs, within twelve years for experienced researchers
Confirm you are not a German national or educational resident, or that you meet the long-term foreign residence test

Check the call opening dates (15 March, 15 July, 15 November) and plan your fellowship start date

Breaching the 90-day-in-18-months Germany residence rule
Missing the career-stage window, where a doctorate older than four years rules out postdoc funding
Formally rejected for incomplete documents or for diverging substantially from the publication list specifications
Choosing a doctoral supervisor or long-term postdoctoral mentor as host, which is generally rejected for lack of further independent academic development
Submitting before the two expert reviews have been uploaded by the reviewers
Missing the German language certificate where German is required for the research
Previously having received direct Humboldt Foundation sponsorship, which bars reapplication to this programme
estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs in Germany beyond the monthly fellowship and family allowances
Tuition or enrolment fees, which this fellowship does not fund
Return travel if the home institution already covers it, or amounts above a single lump sum
Family travel, which is paid only in exceptional circumstances
Costs of research stays outside Germany beyond the 25% guidance, and any earnings there are usually deducted

Confirm key publications are uploaded, with translations or summaries where not in German or English

alerts.message: The current call is closed at capacity. The next call opens 15 November 2026; if you cannot submit in time, work started then counts as received on the portal closure date provided you submit no more than 14 days after the next call opens.
Expect roughly one in four to five applications to be approved, so apply with a strong publication record and a clearly original project.
Applications involving returning to the doctoral supervisor or a longer postdoctoral mentor are generally rejected, so seek a genuinely new academic environment.
Time outside Germany should usually stay under 25% of the funding period, and earnings from the host country are reported and usually deducted.

submission_workflow: Verify your career stage and the 90-day/18-month Germany residence rule

Wait for the expert reviews to be uploaded, then submit the application through the online portal
Monitor the portal status, since the application is only forwarded once the host has submitted their documents
Await the formal eligibility and completeness checks and, if shortlisted, the peer review and selection committee stage
Arrange the pre-stay language course and the fellowship start, two to twelve months after the selection meeting

official.application_cycle: One-semester exchange placement of 4 months at an affiliated Korean university; the page does not publish a specific intake year or application round
official.deadline_note: The NIIED GKS Non-degree Program for Foreign Exchange Students page publishes no application deadline at all. The selection procedure it describes is two-stage and nomination-based: NIIED first selects universities to operate the programme, then NIIED reviews and selects the scholarship applicants recommended by those selected universities. The operative deadline is therefore the home university's internal nomination deadline, which is not published on this page.
official.status_note: The programme is live and its benefits, support period and eligibility are published, but no application window, deadline or open/closed state is published on the official page, so no OPEN/CLOSED determination can be made from it.
official.funding_period: per month for the 4-month (one-semester) support period
official.funding_duration: 4 months (1 semester)
official.tuition_coverage_note: The page describes an exchange placement at an affiliated university and states that the grants cover the expenses for accommodation, settlement, airfare and insurance fee. It makes no statement about tuition fees at the Korean university, so tuition coverage is not recorded.
official.funding_label: 630,000 KRW per month plus round-trip economy class airfare based on the actual cost, for a 4-month (one-semester) support period
benefits: Monthly allowance of 630,000 KRW per month
Round-trip economy class airfare based on the actual cost
Grants described as covering the expenses for accommodation, settlement, airfare and insurance fee

Dual nationals who hold Korean citizenship are not eligible
official.citizenship_residency: Foreign-national undergraduate and graduate (Master's and Doctoral) students enrolled at an overseas university that has an agreement with a NIIED-affiliated Korean university.
official.international_eligibility: Explicitly for foreign-national students; dual nationals holding Korean citizenship are excluded, as are students who have previously received a Korean government scholarship.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Restricted to degree exchange programmes at Korean universities affiliated with NIIED. Students enrolled solely in Korean language courses are excluded.
official.application_method: Nomination-based, two-stage selection. NIIED first selects the universities that will operate the GKS Exchange Students Program, and then NIIED reviews and selects the scholarship applicants recommended by those selected universities. The page does not publish an application form, a portal, a deadline or a document list, so the operative step is nomination by the home university through the bilateral agreement channel.

Home university must have an agreement with a NIIED-affiliated Korean university

No previous Korean government scholarship

official.description: The GKS Non-degree Program for Foreign Exchange Students, administered by the National Institute for International Education (NIIED), the operating institution of the Korean Ministry of Education, offers financial support for selected international exchange students at NIIED-affiliated universities in Korea. The published support period is 4 months (one semester) and the benefits are a monthly allowance of 630,000 KRW plus round-trip economy class airfare at actual cost, with the grants described as covering accommodation, settlement, airfare and insurance. Selection is nomination-based: NIIED selects the operating universities and then reviews and selects applicants recommended by them.
official.program_type: Government exchange scholarship (non-degree, bilateral exchange placement)
official.coverage: Covers a 630,000 KRW monthly allowance and round-trip economy airfare for a one-semester placement, and the page states the grants cover accommodation, settlement, airfare and insurance, but publishes no tuition or general living-cost figure, so it is not recorded as fully funded.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your home university has an agreement with a NIIED-affiliated Korean university - this is the entry gate for the whole route
Confirm your home university is willing and able to nominate you, since NIIED only selects among recommended applicants

Enrolling only in Korean language courses, which the page explicitly excludes
Academic performance below the 80% threshold
Having previously held a Korean government scholarship of any kind
Holding Korean citizenship as a dual national
Missing the home university's internal nomination deadline, which is earlier than any NIIED date and is not published by NIIED
estimated_uncovered_costs: Any tuition or enrolment fees at the Korean university, which the page does not address
Costs above the actual airfare reimbursed, including baggage, seat upgrades and local onward travel
Books, materials, local transport and personal expenses not covered by the 630,000 KRW monthly allowance
Visa and entry costs to Korea
Cost of any extension beyond the 4-month (one-semester) support period

official.application_cycle: Swedish Institute Scholarship for Global Professionals (SISGP), annual round
official.deadline_central_display: The application round is 9-25 February, 14:59 CET on the final day.
official.deadline_note: Applications to the Swedish Institute Scholarship for Global Professionals can be submitted between 9 and 25 February, 14:59 CET on the final day. The institutional dates on the same page are the national university and college admissions periods (1 December to 15 January for the spring round, 1 March to 15 April for the autumn round), which are separate from the scholarship window.
official.status_note: The official Swedish Institute page displays 'Application closed' for the current round, and the 2026 window ended at 14:59 CET on 25 February 2026.
official.funding_duration: 1 to 2 years of full-time study
official.tuition_coverage_note: The scholarship is described by the Swedish Institute as fully funded and covers full tuition fees at a Swedish university or college, plus a monthly living allowance and a travel grant. The page explicitly excludes insurance, family grants and the University Admissions application fee from what the scholarship covers.
official.funding_label: SEK 12,000 per month plus a SEK 15,000 travel grant and full tuition fees
benefits: SEK 12,000 per month as a living allowance
SEK 15,000 as a travel grant to cover initial travel costs to Sweden

A scholarship status that allows a Swedish residence permit to be applied for and gives work rights alongside studies
eligibility: Be a professional with a bachelor's degree or equivalent from an eligible country, or be at most 34 years old and enrolled at an eligible university or college and close to completing a bachelor's degree
Hold the citizenship of, or be a permanent resident of, an eligible country listed on the Swedish Institute page
Be admissible to a Swedish programme, which normally requires at least 100 credits of Swedish or English
Meet the English language requirement: at least 100 credits from a university course, or a result of 4.5 on the TOEFL iBT, 6.0 on the IELTS, or a university record showing comparable English skills
official.citizenship_residency: Citizens of, or permanent residents in, the countries listed as eligible on the Swedish Institute scholarship page. The page publishes the eligible-country list.
official.international_eligibility: Explicit: eligibility is by citizenship or permanent residence in a listed eligible country; the scholarship is aimed at professionals from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Awarded within a subject area and for a specific programme at a Swedish university or college; applicants choose and are ranked by field of study and then by university or college.
official.application_method: Apply through universityadmissions.se during the annual national admission round, and separately answer the scholarship question on the online application form. You apply for a programme, not for the scholarship itself; the scholarship is then awarded among admitted students.
requirements: Apply to a Swedish programme through universityadmissions.se in the spring round
Answer the scholarship question on the online application form
Meet the Swedish Institute's English requirement or the equivalent 100 credits of Swedish or English
Hold the citizenship of or permanent residence in an eligible country
Be a bachelor's degree holder, or within 34 years of age and close to completing a bachelor's degree
Only one university and college may be listed in the application
official.english_requirement: At least 100 credits from a university course, or TOEFL iBT 4.5, IELTS 6.0, or a university record showing comparable English skills
official.english_requirement_note: These figures are published on the Swedish Institute scholarship page as the scholarship's English requirement, and differ from the general universityadmissions.se requirement. The page also notes programmes taught in Swedish require 100 credits of Swedish.
selection_criteria: Applicants are ranked first according to field of study, then according to university or college

award_holder_conditions: The scholarship covers study at a Swedish university or college for the duration of the programme

eligibility: Australian Organisations in partnership with Overseas Counterpart Organisations (OCOs) in eligible developing countries are eligible to apply. 'Individuals cannot apply.'

Examples given include private sector, research centres, higher education providers, VET providers, peak bodies, chambers of commerce, community groups, NGOs, media organisations, professional associations and industry bodies, plus Australian Government departments, agencies, statutory authorities and Government Business Enterprises
Australian Organisations must demonstrate links with OCOs in eligible countries and commit through an in-kind and/or financial co-contribution

A legal representative of the applicant institution, or a person duly authorised by them, must sign. official.description: The Australian Government's Research Training Program funds eligible higher education providers to support research doctorate and research masters students, both domestic and overseas. Students are offered one or more of a tuition fees offset, a stipend for general living costs, and allowances for the ancillary costs of HDR study. Applications are made directly to eligible higher education providers, not to the Department of Education, so no central deadline exists.
official.program_type: Government research training funding
official.coverage: Covers a tuition fees offset, a stipend and ancillary allowances as components decided by the higher education provider; the Department does not state that travel or all required expenses are covered.

Use the RTP FAQs for students (FAQs 3, 5, and 28-30 if applicable) as the Department directs
common_rejection_risks: Assuming there is a single national RTP deadline, when each provider sets its own
Assuming the award is a single bundled package, when students can be offered only one or more of the components
Missing the provider's internal deadline, which is earlier than any national cycle
Not satisfying the provider's academic entry requirements for the research degree
estimated_uncovered_costs: Travel and relocation costs
Any part of tuition not offset by the provider's tuition fees offset
Costs not covered by the stipend, depending on the provider's package and the stipend rate offered

official.description: The Monash International Leadership Scholarship pays 100% of course fees for the duration of an undergraduate degree, with only four awarded per year. It is open to international students from all countries who have received a full, unconditional Monash course offer and intend to enrol full-time at a Monash campus in Australia, and requires no application because eligibility is assessed automatically. Recipients must maintain a Weighted Average Mark of 70 each semester, join the Campus Ambassador Program from their second semester, and provide a student profile for Monash marketing use. The award explicitly excludes overseas student health cover, accommodation and living costs.

official.description: The Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program is a Fulbright exchange that brings mid-career professionals from eligible countries to the United States for one academic year of graduate-level study plus a professional affiliation, organised around four impact areas. Applicants apply through their country's Binational Fulbright Commission or U.S. Embassy, with deadlines varying by country, and final approval rests with the J. official.description: The Clarendon Fund offers over 200 new fully-funded scholarships each year to outstanding graduate scholars at the University of Oxford, covering course fees in full and paying a grant for living expenses. There is no separate scholarship application: candidates are considered automatically if they apply for a new full-time or part-time Master's or DPhil by the December or January admissions deadline for their course, and departments nominate to their division for divisional ranking. Selection criteria are academic record, future potential and aptitude, and student motivation, and successful candidates are usually notified by the end of April.

The scheme is open to new PhD applicants worldwide with no nationality restrictions.

official.coverage: Covers full tuition fees, a GBP 27,036 per year living-cost stipend and a GBP 2,000 per year consumables fund for the first three years, but the stipend is described as assistance with living costs rather than a stated full cost-of-living settlement.

Named sponsors include the Ramon Areces Foundation (all applicants to the Economics and Financial Economics programmes) and the Unicredit Foundation (one full scholarship for Economics or Finance), each covering 100% of tuition, with further sponsors providing full or partial waivers to all Master's applicants. Applications open in October for the following academic year and the first admissions round closes 15 January, with applications completed before that date considered for all funding.
official.program_type: University and sponsor-funded master's scholarships and tuition waivers (merit-based)
official.coverage: Named scholarships cover 100% of tuition fees, and some additional stipend depending on the scholarship; other sponsors provide full or partial tuition waivers. Living costs, travel and insurance are not mentioned as covered.

application_readiness_checklist: Apply in the first round and get a complete file in before 15 January if you want to be considered for all funding
Register in the BSE application system early, since you need the account to start
Prepare a mathematics-heavy statement of purpose that explains your recent mathematical background through courses, research or practical applications
Brief your two referees in advance - letters from professors are strongly preferred, and BSE contacts referees by email after you submit
Arrange the EUR 100 application fee (credit card or Flywire) as part of your submission
Have your language score ready (TOEFL 90, IELTS 6.5, Duolingo 120 or Cambridge 180), or wait until you can provide it
Add a GRE score if you are applying to the PhD Economics Track
common_rejection_risks: Missing 15 January, which limits you to whatever funding is left
An incomplete application because one or both reference letters were never uploaded - the application is not considered complete until both arrive
A weak quantitative background, which BSE calls a key admission criterion alongside academic record and reference letter
Missing the mathematics explanation in the statement of purpose, which BSE calls essential
Applying without a language certificate
Assuming admission guarantees funding - fulfilment of application requirements does not guarantee admission, and aid is merit-based
estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs in Barcelona, which no published award states it covers
Travel and health insurance
Any portion of tuition not covered by a named scholarship or waiver

submission_workflow: Choose up to 3 BSE Master's programs
Create your account in the BSE application system
Complete the application questions, including finance and scholarship details and both referees' details
Upload transcripts, diploma or declaration, CV, statement of purpose, language certificate and passport
Ask both referees to upload their signed letters directly, and remind them to watch for BSE's email
Pay the EUR 100 application fee by credit card or Flywire
Submit before 15 January to be eligible for all funding opportunities

official.description: The TWAS-CSIR Postgraduate Fellowship Programme, run jointly by India's Council of Scientific and Industrial Research and UNESCO-TWAS, funds foreign scholars from developing countries to pursue research toward a PhD in CSIR laboratories and institutes in India. It is restricted to researchers aged 35 or under on 31 December of the application year, nationals of developing countries other than India who hold no residency visa in India or a developed country, holders of an MSc who are employed with a research assignment at home, and who can secure an official acceptance letter from a CSIR host. The fellowship pays a monthly stipend for living costs, food and health insurance plus subsidised accommodation, for up to 4 years full-time or 6 months to 3 years as a sandwich fellowship. The 2026 call closed on 3 June 2026 after an extension from 20 May.

official.description: Invest Your Talent in Italy (IYT), now in its 11th edition, is a scholarship programme of the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, the ICE Agency and Uni-Italia for citizens of 23 listed countries to attend a higher education course in Italy at Master's or Postgraduate level. Winners receive an annual scholarship of EUR 10,800 paid quarterly over a 9-month period starting 1 October 2026, plus exemption from enrolment fees and university contributions, with certain named exceptions. Applications for the 2026-2027 edition ran from 20 April to 11 May 2026 at 6:00pm Italian time and included a compulsory internship at an Italian company or professional association.

official.description: HSG's Excellence Scholarships for Bachelor students are awarded on the basis of merit to students enrolled in a Bachelor's degree at the University of St.Gallen, with the amount corresponding to the current Bachelor-level tuition fees for a total of 6 semesters. Eligibility is not open: the Advice Center for Study Funding identifies enrolled students with outstanding academic performance in the HSG Assessment Year and invites them to apply, and the page states that an application without an invitation from the University of St.Gallen is not possible. Currently HSG and the Monique Dornonville de la Cour - Stiftung award these scholarships in cooperation with the Advice Center, and the final selection rests with the relevant committees.

Missing the invitation or not responding to it
Expecting to self-apply - the page states this is not possible
Additional selection criteria applied by a particular funding source that the candidate does not meet
Confusing this award with the 1 October / 1 March tuition-fee remission scheme and missing the real invitation

official.description: The CERN Research Fellowship offers young physicists, engineers and scientists a contract of 6 to 24 months, extendable to 36 months, with a net monthly stipend of CHF 7,004 or CHF 7,425 depending on degree and years of post-graduation experience. The package includes CERN health insurance, a pension contribution, an installation grant, family/child/infant allowances, travel to Geneva, 30 days paid leave plus 2 weeks of annual closure, and training including language classes. Recruitment is per advertised vacancy and is limited to nationals of CERN Member and Associate Member States, with annual exceptions.

official.coverage: A net monthly salary plus CERN health insurance, pension contribution, installation grant, family/child/infant allowances, travel to Geneva, paid leave and training; there is no tuition element because fellows are employees rather than fee-paying students.

official.deadline_central_display: Fellowship positions may be advertised through calls for expressions of interest, published on our career website or via WIPO's LinkedIn or other social media channels.
official.deadline_note: There is no single programme deadline. WIPO states fellowship positions may be advertised through calls for expressions of interest published on its career website or on LinkedIn and other social media channels, so the closing date is set per call.

official.travel_coverage_note: Relocation assistance: WIPO will cover travel expenses at the start and end of your fellowship, and if necessary WIPO assists in facilitating visa formalities to Switzerland.

official.description: WIPO's Fellowship Program places young professionals at the Organization in Geneva for 12 to 36 months across four fellow categories: translation, legal case management, visiting and research, and other specialized roles. Fellows receive a monthly stipend of CHF 3,000 to 8,000 depending on background and experience, medical and accident insurance, holiday and leave entitlements, and covered relocation travel with visa facilitation. Positions are advertised through calls for expressions of interest on WIPO's career website and social channels, so there is no single programme deadline.

official.tuition_coverage_note: SPF covers full tuition for six semesters. Renewal for a maximum of six semesters depends on a minimum term GPA of 3.0, with no separate tuition waiver for the renewed period stated beyond that.
official.living_cost_coverage_note: SPF pays a monthly stipend of KRW 1,500,000 to 2,000,000 for 3 to 4 years, and the published benefits also include round-trip airfare economy from the home country to Korea, Korean language training, national health insurance, and child care support. official.description: The SNU President Fellowship Program supports newly admitted PhD students at Seoul National University who are instructional staff at major universities in developing countries, and spouses of doctoral students of developing-country nationals, among other tracks. It covers full tuition for six semesters, a monthly stipend of KRW 1,500,000 to 2,000,000 for 3 to 4 years, round-trip airfare, Korean language training, national health insurance, child care support and a return settlement allowance, renewable for up to six semesters on a 3.0 minimum GPA. For the Spring 2027 intake the online application ran 6 to 9 July 2026 and documents were due 6 to 31 July 2026.

official.description: The ISTA PhD program is described as a fully-funded, interdisciplinary, English-taught doctoral programme in which PhD students are employed by the Institute of Science and Technology Austria and receive internationally competitive salaries and full social security coverage, with no tuition fees and no application fee. Students enter with a Bachelor's or Master's degree in biology, neuroscience, mathematics, computer science, physics, chemistry or a related area, and choose among seven tracks. The programme runs in two phases around a qualifying exam, requires coursework of 30 ECTS (short route) or 42 ECTS (long route), teaching assistance, biannual progress reviews and annual thesis presentations, and a thesis defense typically within three to four years of passing the qualifying exam. Applications for the 2027 call open in late October and close on 8 January 2027.

official.description: Kyushu University does not operate a single named international scholarship for master's and PhD students. Instead, it publishes an annual scholarship information list in which more than 65 awards from external foundations are available to enrolled international students, each with its own stipend amount, duration, deadline and application route. Some awards are made through on-campus selection by the International Student Exchange Division and others require direct application to the foundation. Amounts published for the 2027 cycle range from JPY 50,000 per month to JPY 200,000 per month, plus tuition subsidies in some cases.
official.program_type: University-administered external foundation scholarship list
official.coverage: Most listed awards are monthly stipends only; a minority state tuition subsidies or full academic cost coverage, and none of the published entries state coverage of living costs, travel or health insurance for the foundation awards.

If applying directly, contact the student affairs office of your department or graduate school for a scholarship recommendation form
Note that several on-campus awards require documents in Japanese, handwritten by the applicant
common_rejection_risks: Applying after the award's own deadline, which is separate per award and often in September or October
Missing a Japanese language requirement where the award's documents must be in Japanese
Failing the on-campus eligibility conditions, such as a residence card whose stay does not run to 1 April 2027
Holding other scholarships that breach the adjustment or exclusivity rules, such as the Heiwa Nakajima prohibition on combining awards
Missing a mandatory interview or written examination, which cannot be rescheduled

official.description: Manaaki New Zealand Scholarships is the New Zealand Government scholarship programme, administered by Education New Zealand, for citizens of its partner countries to study in New Zealand. It covers four types of award - undergraduate and postgraduate tertiary study, Thematic Short Term Training Scholarships, Vocational Short Term Training Scholarships, and English Language Training for Officials Scholarships. Applicants are exempt if they previously completed an English-taught programme in Australia, English-speaking Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the United Kingdom or the United States.

official.description: The KU Leuven Inspiring the Outstanding Scholarship is a merit-based scholarship for students of all nationalities applying to a KU Leuven master's programme, restricted to those whose previous degrees were obtained outside Flanders and who are not already enrolled at a Flemish institution. It combines a full tuition fee waiver with an allowance of EUR 13,200 per academic year for a maximum of two academic years, and requires both a complete master's application file including the Candidacy Form and a separate online scholarship registration by 15 January 2026 at 23.59 CET. Nominees are then interviewed by video and ranked by a central KU Leuven Selection Committee.

official.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are prestigious international master's programmes jointly designed and delivered by at least three higher education institutions in at least three countries, with additional academic and non-academic partners. Students apply directly to the institution running the programme, and the best-ranked applicants worldwide can receive full scholarships that cover participation costs and contribute to travel, visa and a living allowance. Degrees run 1-2 academic years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS) and yield either a joint degree or at least two national degrees.

selection_criteria: Academic excellence (weight 50%): as demonstrated by past academic results, transcripts, awards and distinctions. Indicators: academic record; scholarships and awards held; duration of previous studies; type of program and courses pursued; relative standing if available

Research potential (weight 30%): as demonstrated by research history, interest in discovery, the proposed research, its potential contribution to the advancement of knowledge in the field and any anticipated outcomes. Indicators: quality and originality of contributions to research and development; relevance of work experience and academic training to the field of proposed research; significance, feasibility and merit of proposed research; sound judgment and ability to think critically; ability to apply skills and knowledge; initiative and autonomy; research experience and achievements relative to expectations of someone with your academic experience

Personal characteristics and interpersonal skills (weight 20%): as demonstrated by past professional and relevant extracurricular interactions and collaborations. Indicators: work experience; leadership experience; project management including organizing conferences and meetings; ability or potential to communicate theoretical, technical or scientific concepts clearly and logically in written and oral formats; involvement in academic life; volunteerism and community outreach

official.description: The Canada Graduate Research Scholarship - Master's (CGRS M) is one of three programs in the Canada Research Training Awards Suite, jointly administered by CIHR, NSERC and SSHRC, and it supports up to 3,298 students annually across all disciplines. The value is $27,000 for 12 months, and the merit review is conducted by the host institution against published weights of academic excellence 50%, research potential 30% and personal characteristics and interpersonal skills 20%. Applicants must be Canadian citizens, permanent residents or Protected Persons as of the deadline, and must have completed 0 to 12 months of full-time study in the program for which funding is requested. Applications go through the Research Portal to up to three institutions by 1 December before 8:00 pm ET, and offers are available in the portal from 1 April with alternate offers possible until 31 January of the following year.

official.description: The Canada-ASEAN Scholarships and Educational Exchanges for Development (SEED) program is a short-term exchange offered by Global Affairs Canada, enabling students from ASEAN member states to conduct study or research at a Canadian post-secondary institution in areas that contribute to the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. It provides 10,200 CAD for four months or one academic term, funding eligible expenses including airfare, health insurance, living expenses, ground transportation and books. Canadian institutions apply on behalf of candidates through My EduCanada, and the 2025 application period is closed.
official.program_type: Government-to-government scholarship (exchange)
official.coverage: Covers 10,200 CAD for four months or one academic term, applicable to visa or permit fees, airfare, health insurance, living expenses, ground transportation, and books and supplies; college and undergraduate tuition fees are waived through a required student exchange agreement, and graduate study does not require an agreement.

official.description: The UCAS Scholarship for International Students offers non-Chinese students funding to study at the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences or a CAS institute. The Full Scholarship bundles a tuition waiver (PhD RMB 40,000/year, Master's RMB 30,000/year), a monthly stipend (PhD RMB 2,500, Master's RMB 2,000, topped up by host assistantship to at least RMB 3,500 and RMB 3,000 respectively), basic accommodation, RMB 800/year medical insurance and a RMB 600 application fee waiver, for up to 36 months without extension; a Partial Scholarship covers tuition, insurance and the fee waiver only. PhD and Master's applications closed on 31 January 2026, while visiting student categories are open-ended.

Selection combines file quality, interview, and Advisory Board and Panel review, with final awards confirmed in four waves between May and July 2027 conditional on admission to a French institution.

official.description: The Padua International Excellence Scholarship offers up to 76 scholarships to high-achieving international students enrolling in an English-taught bachelor's or master's degree at the University of Padua. Each award is EUR 8,000 gross per academic year plus exemption from student fees, leaving only the regional fee and revenue stamp payable. There is no separate application: applying to the degree programme by the deadline enters the candidate into the competition, and each course's Teaching Committee selects the winner.
official.program_type: University scholarship
official.coverage: Covers EUR 8,000 gross per year plus tuition fee exemption, but not living costs, travel or the regional fee and revenue stamp.

official.description: The University of Bologna's study grants and subsidies framework is a portfolio rather than a single scholarship. It combines fee exemptions and reductions (merit-based total exemption for first-year second cycle students who graduated on time with top marks, ERGO means-tested reductions, disability, parenthood and family enrolments), ER.GO regional study grants, '150 hour' collaboration grants, mobility scholarships, and specific international schemes including a reduced fixed fee for citizens of poor, developing and non-EU/non-OECD countries, Unibo for Refugees and MUR-CRUI refugee scholarships. Individual calls and deadlines are published on the University's bandi.unibo.it portal.
official.program_type: University fee exemptions, tuition-fee reductions and regional/national study grants administered through published calls
official.coverage: Predominantly tuition-fee reductions and exemptions, plus ER.GO study grants which the Region says bear the cost of your academic studies; accommodation, canteen, transport and software benefits are separate services rather than part of the grants.

eligibility: Be a citizen of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan, as of 1 April of the fellowship's fiscal year and during the fellowship period (JSPS treats Taiwanese and Palestinian researchers in this manner)

Have obtained a doctoral degree within six years of the date the fellowship goes into effect, counting from 2 April six years prior to the fiscal year, or be expected to receive a PhD by the start date of the fellowship period
Not be a Japanese citizen and not be a foreigner permitted permanent residence in Japan

official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All fields of the humanities, social sciences and natural sciences. official.application_method: Selection runs through two channels, Open Calls and Nominations. In the Open Call, heads of Japanese universities or research institutions apply to invite foreign researchers, and a selection process designates the Fellows. In the Nomination channel, overseas nominating authorities recommend candidates. Host researchers submit through JSPS's electronic application system. Each host researcher may submit up to three applications.

official.description: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan (Standard) invite young overseas researchers to conduct collaborative research at universities and research institutions in Japan for 12 to 24 months in any field of the humanities, social sciences and natural sciences. Each round awards about 120 fellowships, providing a JPY 362,000 monthly maintenance allowance, a round-trip air ticket, a JPY 200,000 settling-in allowance and overseas travel insurance. Applicants are selected either by a Japanese host institution through the Open Call or through an overseas nominating authority.
official.program_type: Government research fellowship
official.coverage: Covers a JPY 362,000 monthly allowance, round-trip airfare, a JPY 200,000 settling-in allowance and overseas travel insurance; no tuition is listed because the fellow is hosted at a research institution rather than enrolled in a degree programme.

official.description: The Bekker NAWA Programme supports the international mobility of PhD students, scientists and academic teachers from Polish scientific units by funding research fellowships of 3 to 24 months at recognised research centres and academic institutions worldwide, excluding the Russian Federation. The fellowship covers living costs in the host country plus a mobility allowance, as flat-rate sums, with top-ups for dependants. Applications are submitted through NAWA's IT system in English, one per call.

official.description: The Lane Kirkland Scholarship Program, founded by the Polish-American Freedom Foundation and financially supported by the Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange (NAWA), supports graduates from Ukraine, Belarus, Russia, Moldova, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan who have at least two years' professional experience and are determined to be involved in the development of democracy, economy and civil society. Grantees study for two semesters at one of five Polish academic centres, complete two semester papers and a diploma paper, and undertake a professional internship of at least two weeks, supported by a PLN 18,000 stipend plus accommodation, insurance, a return ticket, transport, visa costs and a Polish language course.

official.application_cycle: Rolling, academic-year based. The study.gov.pl page describes the Erasmus+ programme period as 2014 to 2020 and is out of date; current rules are on the European Commission's Erasmus+ site.
official.deadline_institutional: Varies by sending institution and receiving institution; each institution sets its own internal selection and application dates, and the European Commission publishes none centrally.
official.deadline_note: There is no central application form or central deadline. The European Commission states: 'There's no central application form to study abroad with Erasmus+. You can reach out to the international or Erasmus+ office of your university or higher education institution to start the process. Your sending higher education institution is obliged to select applicants in a fair and transparent way.' The deadline therefore belongs to the sending institution, and each receiving institution has its own admission deadlines that may fall months before the mobility starts.
official.status_note: Erasmus+ is a standing EU programme rather than a single annual call. The European Commission's 'Studying abroad' page was last updated 18 December 2025 and describes a continuous process through sending institutions. The Polish national agency page (study.gov.pl/erasmus) is live but describes the programme as running 2014 to 2020 and contains no current figures.
official.funding_period: per mobility period, set by national grant agreements
official.funding_duration: long-term mobility 2 to 12 months; short-term mobility 5 to 30 days (blended); maximum total 12 months within one study cycle; up to 24 months for one-cycle courses such as medicine or architecture
official.tuition_coverage_note: 'As an Erasmus+ student, you are exempt from fees for tuition, registration, examinations, and charges for access to laboratories or libraries at the receiving institution. Small fees for insurance or student union membership may still apply.'

official.citizenship_residency: Not citizenship-based at EU level. The relevant test is registration at a higher education institution that participates in the Erasmus+ programme, which in practice means enrolment in a Programme Country institution; mobility is possible within Erasmus+ programme countries and to and from associated countries.
official.international_eligibility: Erasmus+ student mobility is not a third-country study-abroad scholarship. Traineeships abroad are open to students enrolled in higher education in a Programme Country, and are also open to recent graduates. The European Commission publishes a downloadable list of higher education institutions holding an Erasmus Charter for 2021-2027.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Sending and receiving institutions must hold an inter-institutional agreement; both must hold the Erasmus Charter for Higher Education (for institutions in EU Member States or third countries associated with Erasmus+, with non-associated third country institutions committing to the Charter's principles when signing).
official.application_method: There is no central application. Contact the international or Erasmus+ office of your own (sending) university. The sending institution selects applicants in a fair and transparent way, applies for funding on students' behalf, and students then sign a participant grant agreement. Before the mobility a 'learning agreement for studies' is signed with sending and receiving institutions, along with the Erasmus+ Student Charter.

official.english_requirement_note: No English requirement is published for Erasmus+ student mobility. The European Commission directs students to Erasmus+ Online Language Support and states that the grant amount depends on living-cost differences between the home and destination country; language requirements are set by the receiving institution.
selection_criteria: Fair and transparent selection by the sending higher education institution (the Commission states this obligation but publishes no criteria)
official.duration: Long-term mobility: minimum 2 months to a maximum 12 months abroad, including blended mobilities with a virtual component. Short-term mobility: 5 to 30 days, and these must be blended mobilities. Maximum total duration 12 months within one study cycle, and more than one exchange is possible within that limit. Only doctoral candidates may do a short-term mobility without a virtual component. For 'one-cycle' courses such as medicine or architecture, up to 24 months.

official.description: Erasmus+ is the European Union programme supporting projects, partnerships, events and mobility in education, training, youth and sport. For individual students its main actions are studying abroad, traineeships abroad and the Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degrees. There is no central application form or central deadline: applications run through the sending university, which selects students fairly and transparently and applies for the funding. Students are exempt from tuition, registration, examination and laboratory/library fees at the receiving institution and receive a grant contributing to travel and daily living costs, with the amount set by national grant agreements.
official.program_type: EU programme grant / mobility scholarship (inter-institutional, no central application)
official.region: European Union and Erasmus+ associated countries (the record's 'Poland' refers to the Polish national agency page, not to a Polish-only scheme)
official.coverage: Erasmus+ covers exemption from tuition, registration, examination and laboratory/library access fees at the receiving institution plus a grant contributing to travel and daily living costs, but the grant is a contribution whose amount depends on living-cost differences, applicant numbers and distance, and small insurance or student-union fees may still apply - so it is not a full cost-of-living package.

common_rejection_risks: Missing your sending institution's internal selection round, which is typically earlier than the receiving university's deadline
Proposing a mobility that is not part of your degree programme and therefore not creditable
Applying to a receiving institution that has no inter-institutional agreement with your university
Assuming the grant covers full living costs - it is a contribution, not a cost-of-living package
For non-EU nationals, visa and travel costs not covered by the grant

official.deadline_note: This is an umbrella record for the Fulbright Program in Poland, which runs several distinct awards with different application windows. The Polish-U.S. Fulbright Commission publishes only month ranges per award, not exact dates: Graduate Student Award February-April, Junior Research Award May-October, Polish Scholar Award February-May, STEM Impact Award February-May, Polish Studies Award May-September, Schuman Award September-December. For grants to Poland (US citizens), the U.S. and Polish deadlines are set by the U.S. Department of State and the commission respectively, and are not published as exact dates on the commission pages read.
official.status_note: The commission's site carries a 30 September 2026 news item on the Fulbright Specialist Program 2025-26, an invitation for the 'To Poland for Science' conference on 19 October 2026 and a September 2026 announcement of Fulbright Scholar-in-Residence grantees for 2026-27, indicating live cycles. official.description: The Fulbright Program in Poland, initiated in 1959 and administered by the Polish-U.S. Fulbright Commission, is a merit-based exchange programme jointly funded by the governments of Poland and the United States. It runs distinct awards in both directions: grants to Poland for US citizens (Scholar, Student, English Teaching Assistant, Specialist, Schuman) and grants to the USA for Polish citizens (Graduate Student up to USD 47,000 for a first year, Junior Research, Polish Scholar, Polish Studies, STEM Impact). official.description: The PSC Scholarship is the Singapore Government's premier merit scholarship, awarding varied career pathways in the Public Service across Public Administration, Professional Service and Uniformed Service tracks. It covers the cost of degree (tuition fees and other approved charges, plus return airfare for overseas degrees), maintenance and other allowances, and sponsors PSC development programmes including the Preparatory Course, the Mid-Course Programme with an internship, a possible Gap Year and the Public Service Leadership Programme. Holders serve a bond of 4 to 6 years depending on the country of study, and applications for the 2027 cycle are open and close on 15 March 2027.

official.coverage: Covers tuition fees and other approved charges, return airfare for overseas degrees, maintenance and other allowances (full salary for Uniformed Service holders), development programmes, approved exchanges and a sponsored master's if requirements are met, in exchange for a 4 to 6 year public service bond.

official.description: The Lee Kuan Yew Scholarship, set up in 1991 by the Tanjong Pagar Citizens' Consultative Committee with public funding, is Singapore's premier postgraduate scholarship and is open to Singapore citizens. Recipients receive full tuition fees coverage and an annual allowance of S$50,000 for up to 2 years for a Master's degree or up to 5 years for PhD studies, with no restrictions on the course of study and no bond, though recipients are expected to contribute to Singapore society. Applications are submitted through the PSC Gateway portal with a published deadline of 28 February, and the page states applications for the 2026 award are closed.

official.description: The MOE Teaching Scholarship/Award (Full-Term) sponsors Singapore Citizen students who intend to become teachers, covering undergraduate tuition fees and other approved charges plus a monthly maintenance allowance at a reputable local or overseas university, in exchange for a teaching service bond of 4 to 6 years. Applicants are considered across the full range of MOE Teaching Scholarships and Awards, and a parallel PSC Scholarship (Teaching Service) offers airfare and possible postgraduate sponsorship. Application windows are opened separately for each qualification type rather than on a single programme-wide date.

MOE does not itemise personal living costs, and it does not use the phrase 'fully funded'.

official.description: The A*STAR International Fellowship supports up to 2 years of overseas postdoctoral training at a leading overseas university, research institution or deep-tech startup, in one of two tracks: AIF (Research) and AIF (Innovation). Support comprises a monthly overseas living allowance (SGD 5,000 for Singapore Citizens), a monthly sustenance allowance, annual return airfare, one-off and annual allowances, and personal insurance. Awardees must return to Singapore and contribute to A*STAR for 3 years after training.

official.description: The National Science Scholarship (PhD) develops top researchers for Singapore by funding up to five years of PhD study at top international institutions, with a compulsory one-year research attachment at an A*STAR research institute before the PhD begins. Support covers full tuition fees, a monthly sustenance allowance of SGD 4,500 for Singapore Citizens or SGD 4,100 for Permanent Residents, a monthly overseas living allowance, annual return airfare and several other allowances. Applicants apply in one of two annual cycles closing 1 April and 1 October, and scholars serve a four-year work-back commitment in Singapore, reduced to three years if the PhD is completed in a non-anglophone country.

SIT states each scholarship is valued up to S$18,030 per annum including an annual stipend of S$7,200, plus a one-time laptop allowance of S$2,000 and a possible one-time Global Mobility Grant of S$10,000. It forms part of Temasek's S$150 million 'T-Spring' community gift announced in 2024 for Temasek's 50th anniversary.

official.description: The SUTD Trailblazers Scholarship is open to Singapore Citizens applying for admission to SUTD's undergraduate degree programme who have outstanding GCE 'A' level, Local Polytechnic Diploma, NUS High School Diploma, IB Diploma or Year 12 equivalent qualifications and demonstrate strong leadership. It covers subsidised tuition fees after the Tuition Grant for the normal duration of the programme, up to four years, plus an annual allowance of S$6,000 paid as S$3,000 per academic term, and a travel award of up to S$5,000 for approved overseas programmes. Recipients must achieve and maintain good academic standing, complete at least 20 hours of service to the University, and take up the Tuition Grant Scheme; no bond is attached.

official.application_method: Tick the corresponding box on the EPFL Bachelor application form before 30 April and provide the requested application file. Where the applicant is eligible, an ad hoc form is issued and the listed documents are requested. Each section then pre-selects the best applications for a presentation of the maturity project (or another subject, if not applicable) before a jury made up in part of EPFL academic staff, in a short five-minute presentation followed by questions. The applications retained are then examined by the Central Committee for Bachelor Excellence Fellowships, which awards the fellowships.

official.description: EPFL's Bachelor Excellence Fellowships are offered to holders of a Swiss high-school maturity diploma and holders of a Swiss vocational maturity diploma undertaking the CMS, and to any applicant to an EPFL Bachelor programme who meets one of four published status or schooling conditions. The fellowship is worth CHF 10,000 spread over three years, paid as six semester instalments, and comes with a guaranteed room reservation in an EPFL partner residence on request and at the student's own cost, plus an excellence certificate. Applications are made by ticking a box on the Bachelor application form before 30 April, followed by section pre-selection, a five-minute jury presentation of the maturity project, and a decision by the Central Committee for Bachelor Excellence Fellowships at the end of June.

Grants cover the grantee's salary plus the project funds needed, and run for a maximum of four years, with project starts between 1 September 2027 and 1 September 2028. Applicants may be from Switzerland or abroad provided they meet a four-year (nine-year for medical graduates) post-qualification window and a link with Switzerland. The Call 2026 opened 3 August 2026 and closes 3 November 2026 at 17:00 CET.

official.description: The SNSF Starting Grants are the SNSF's highest level of career funding, enabling researchers to carry out their own independent project and lead a research team in Switzerland. Applicants can request a budget of up to 1 million francs for project funding over five years and can additionally apply for funds to cover their own salary. Eligibility requires a doctorate (or equivalent or medical degree), falling within the eligibility window, not yet having achieved the objective of the call, and a Swiss link of at least two years of research at an average of at least 80% worktime. Evaluation is a two-phase, competition-based procedure with external peer review and interviews.
official.program_type: Career-stage research grant (highest level of SNSF career funding), including the applicant's own salary
official.coverage: Funds an independent research project and team leadership in Switzerland: up to CHF 1 million project funding over five years plus, on request, the applicant's own salary. It is a research grant rather than a student funding package, so tuition and personal living costs are not items it covers.

official.deadline_note: The MOE publishes a recurring annual deadline rather than a dated calendar deadline: 'Applications for an STRA to undertake a research project in Taiwan in the following year must be submitted to a university, or tertiary college in Taiwan, or a research organization affiliated with the MOE ... at which the applicant would like to undertake research (referred to below as the host institution). Applications must arrive at the host institution no later than September 30 each year.' Because the application is lodged with the chosen host institution, the deadline is simultaneously the MOE central deadline and the institutional deadline; individual host institutions may set earlier internal dates. No specific year is stated on the page, which carries an original date of 2020-12-08 and was still live on 1 October 2026.
